correctness.rationale: Under the passive linear Lindblad dynamics a coherent pulse evolves with the dissipative two-mode amplitude matrix; the normally ordered number covariance starts at zero and remains zero under vacuum loss. Subtracting the scalar mean frequency minus iγ/4 gives a traceless matrix with square Z²I; its exponential gives B=−Fg sin(Zt)exp(−γt/4−iω̄t)/Z. The modulus squared is the stated damped cosh-minus-cos expression, with no positive-time zeros when β=2|Im Z|>0. Off resonance Im(Z²)=−γΔ/4, so β>0. Taking the Hermitian part of the amplitude generator gives nonpositive real eigenvalue parts; equality would force the charger's eigenvector component to vanish, inconsistent with g>0. Consequently β<α. The derivative is a positive factor times R cos(ϖt−φ)−L(t), where L=α cosh(βt)−β sinh(βt)>0 and φ=atan2(ϖ,α). L starts below R, decreases then grows strictly to infinity; writing it as a shifted cosh gives the exact unique positive envelope crossing T_env. Beyond it the energy strictly decreases. An independent lobe count controls the residual: roots that can yield a maximum lie in positive cosine lobes; there the derivative sign function is strictly concave, since its second derivative is −ϖ²R cos(ϖt−φ)−β²L<0. Every full lobe with center before T_env starts and ends negative and is positive at the center, hence contributes exactly one strict maximum. There is at most one per lobe and none starting after T_env. Only a bounded number of initial or terminal lobes can differ from the center count, even at envelope equality or tangency. Thus N=ϖ T_env/(2π)+O(1). Expanding at fixed g,γ gives ϖ=2G+O(Δ²), β=γ|Δ|/(4G)+O(|Δ|³), and R/α→4g/γ with O(Δ²) error. The artanh term divided by β stays bounded, yielding the claimed coefficient and additive error. At resonance, the derivative of exp(−γt/2) sin²(Gt) gives one strict maximum per period and the displayed zero nodes. A separately written numerical lobe replay gives N=26,50,124,247 at Δ=0.1,0.05,0.02,0.01 with g=γ=1, matching the frozen report; this is supplementary. The uploaded script was not executed.
residual_risks: The analytic proof, not finite root bracketing, decides all-detuning finiteness, tangencies and the remainder. Off-resonant positivity is for t>0, not t=0. The remainder is at fixed g>γ/4 and γ>0; it does not justify a joint approach to the exceptional point.

evidence: The earlier telegraph proof already differentiates a damped two-exponential sum, counts contributing positive cosine lobes by strict concavity, and squeezes the scaled count. That establishes the method and leading-scale behavior in the stationary dephasing model. The compared pulsed battery paper supplies the resonance formula only.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A parameter rename in the stationary theorem would leave its nonzero initial coherence and unequal modal weights intact. Here the physically fixed zero initial battery amplitude produces equal opposite modal coefficients, giving the cosh-minus-cos energy and a closed envelope threshold. Computing that exact crossing and controlling the endpoint-lobe error are needed for the quantitative bounded-error claim; the earlier scaled limit by itself does not imply that error.

evidence: Writing z=iZ for the pulse transfer (up to branch choice), a=γ/4, v²=g²+Δ²/4 and ε=γΔ/(8v) identifies z²=a²−v²+2ivε with the telegraph discriminant. Under this correspondence the earlier limiting coefficient has the same cosh-threshold form and matches the leading cavity expression in the limit.

The pulse amplitude is proportional to exp(−at)sinh(zt), which vanishes at zero, whereas stationary telegraph dephasing gives exp(−at)[cosh(zt)+(a+ivε/a)sinh(zt)/z], which starts at one. Their mode weights and exact derivative envelopes differ.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Positive-revival components of a nonzero modulus and positive-derivative components of its square count in essentially the same way as strict maxima for these analytic lobe problems. The spectral identification therefore shows real method-level overlap, not merely similar words. It does not identify the observables or turn the stationary-telegraph theorem into an exact formula for the initially empty battery.

originality.rationale: The contribution supported is the all-time classification for the charger-pulsed, amplitude-damped, initially empty battery, including the closed detuned cutoff and an additive O(1) count with the explicit model normalization. The resonant baseline, two-mode spectrum and the general cosine-versus-growing-envelope mechanism are not novel. The strongest indexed telegraph analogue shares both the counting idea and the functional form of the leading coefficient under spectral identification, but its published assertion fixes stationary initial data for a different observable and supplies a scaled limit, not this cutoff or bounded-error cavity count.
residual_risks: The bounded search does not exclude a preexisting general two-mode extremum theorem with arbitrary initial modal weights and an additive count bound, or an equivalent older damped-oscillator treatment. The counting technique and abstract inverse-parameter pattern must be credited to the directly inspected analogue; no absolute historical priority is established.

value.rationale: The sharp count and closed final-turning bound distinguish a singular resonance idealization from free decay under any fixed nonzero detuning in a canonical pulsed model. The explicit envelope yields an all-time stopping bound without arbitrarily truncating a transient simulation, and the error bound quantifies how many exact peaks are lost as detuning changes. This is not merely diagonalization, a new name for the telegraph law, or a fit to a finite peak count.
residual_risks: Exact extrema at late times can be exponentially small; the result is not a prediction for experimentally detectable cycles or for models with direct battery loss or continuous drive.
